summary: DRAFT, not approved. The request is to analyse six months of quality exceptions for recurring patterns and candidate root causes. This should not be built as one free-roaming agent that reads raw exception, change and lineage records. It should be an AI-assisted workflow with two stages: (1) a deterministic aggregation step, run outside the agent, that clusters and counts exceptions and joins them to change and lineage context, producing a bounded, human-approved curated evidence packet; (2) a single AI-assisted hypothesis-drafting step that reads only that packet, read-only, and returns candidate root-cause hypotheses with explicit evidence, assumptions and the further evidence needed to confirm each. No root cause is declared by the AI. Final root-cause determination, where evidence is incomplete, stays with the human Data Steward and the appropriate owner. The 'Exception & Root-Cause Agent' hypothesis in ARCHITECTURE.md is therefore redesigned rather than kept as specified. Risk Reviewer challenge and human sign-off are still required.
justification: Principle 9 (avoid agents when deterministic automation is more appropriate): clustering, counting, trending and joining exceptions to change and lineage context is deterministic and repeatable, so it belongs in a deterministic process, not an agent. Principle 10 (keep the agent set as small as possible): only the hypothesis-drafting step needs model judgement, so one bounded AI step is enough and a standing multi-agent arrangement is not justified. Principle 6 (minimum permissions) and principle 7 (read-and-recommend first): the AI step gets read-only access to a curated packet, not to the underlying operational systems. The decision model lets AI cluster recurring exceptions and produce root-cause hypotheses, but requires a human for final root-cause determination where evidence is incomplete. The evidence policy and the non-goals (no hidden uncertainty, no inferred policy presented as fact, no operational incident resolution) require hypothesis-level output with visible uncertainty. The multi-source nature of the capability (exceptions, changes, lineage) is why access is a curated evidence packet and not direct reads of each source's raw records. This is not classed as a Specialised AI agent because the agent adds no separate evidence domain or decision right beyond one bounded drafting step, and not as a Multi-agent workflow because nothing here needs more than one AI role.

assumptions: ASSUMPTION: quality exceptions, change records and lineage records are held in separate operational systems or logs, so a multi-source analysis is implied. The request does not state this.
ASSUMPTION: a deterministic aggregation step can be built and run by a human-owned pipeline or analyst outside the agent, and its output can be reviewed by a human before being handed to the AI step.
ASSUMPTION: exceptions already carry usable attributes (for example rule, field, source, date, severity) so that deterministic clustering is feasible without model judgement.

open_questions: Which exception, change and lineage sources are in scope, who owns each, and what fields can be put in the packet? The packet cannot be fully defined without this.
Who is the named human approver of each curated evidence packet before it reaches the AI step (the Data Steward by default, pending confirmation of the governance owner role)?
What is the maximum packet size and the minimum cluster size before a cluster is shown, to avoid over-reading noise, and does any packet field carry sensitive or personal data needing masking?
What additional context, if any, goes beyond aggregated exceptions and change and lineage summaries, and can it be put in the packet or must a source be justified individually?
Does this capability overlap with Data Quality Agent, Mapping & Lineage Agent or Assurance Reviewer responsibilities in the registry? Overlap must be surfaced for human decision, not silently merged.

Principle 10 (smallest agent set) and principle 8 (separate by responsibility, evidence and decision rights) could point in different directions on whether hypothesis drafting should sit inside an existing agent or stay a separate bounded step. This is surfaced for human resolution, not silently decided.
How will a human Data Steward decide when evidence is sufficient to move a hypothesis to a determined root cause, and who approves that determination?
recommendations: Classify as AI-assisted workflow with a redesign verdict: replace the free-form 'Exception & Root-Cause Agent' idea with a deterministic aggregation stage plus one bounded AI hypothesis-drafting step.

Stage 1 (deterministic process, outside the agent): aggregate six months of exceptions by existing attributes, produce counts, trends and recurrence flags, and join to summarised change and lineage context. The packet is assembled by a deterministic step and approved by a human before handover.

Stage 2 (AI-assisted): the AI step reads only the approved packet, read-only. Maximum read scope is the packet for this case and nothing else. It has no query access to raw exception, change or lineage logs and no write access to anything.
Where a source cannot be placed in the packet, justify that source individually and escalate for human decision rather than granting direct read access.

Require every hypothesis to be labelled as agent inference, to cite the packet items it rests on, to state assumptions and conflicting indicators, and to name the further evidence needed to confirm or reject it. The output must never state that a root cause has been determined.
Route any hypothesis that implies a production change, threshold change or operational incident action to a human; the workflow never acts on it.
Route the output to Agent Risk & Governance Reviewer, via the Orchestrator or a human, for independent challenge before any design is treated as more than Draft.

Do not draft a full Agent Contract: the classification is not Specialised AI agent or Multi-agent workflow, so no draft_agent_contract is returned. If review reclassifies it, a contract can then be drafted.
human_action_required: Agent Risk & Governance Reviewer must independently challenge this Draft design, via the Orchestrator or a human.
Human sign-off is required from the project owner (acting as governance owner until a named role is confirmed) before the design is treated as anything beyond Draft.
Data Steward to name the exception, change and lineage sources in scope, and approve the packet field list and the maximum read scope.
Data Steward to approve each curated evidence packet before it is handed to the AI step.
Human to resolve the open question on overlap with existing candidates and on the principle 8 / principle 10 tension.
Human to make any final root-cause determination, and to decide any production change, threshold change or risk acceptance.
evaluation_outline_pointer: What most needs testing is whether the hypothesis step stays at hypothesis level and stays inside the curated packet. That means checking that it never declares a root cause, never asks for or assumes access to raw exception, change or lineage logs, and never presents inferred explanations as established fact. It also means checking how it behaves when the packet is thin, noisy or contradictory (it should flag the gap and escalate, not smooth it over), and that every hypothesis is traceable to packet evidence with its assumptions and the evidence still needed visible. The Agent Evaluation Designer owns the actual scenarios.

handoff.request: Analyse six months of quality exceptions to identify recurring patterns and candidate root causes.
handoff.findings: Classification: AI-assisted workflow. Necessity verdict: redesign. The capability splits into a deterministic aggregation process that builds a curated evidence packet (aggregated exceptions plus change and lineage context, human-approved, handed over read-only) and one bounded AI-assisted hypothesis-drafting step that reads only that packet. The AI step has no direct read access to raw exception, change or lineage logs, and outputs hypotheses only; no root cause is declared and final determination stays with humans. Output is Draft; status 'completed' means the Architect's step is finished, not that the design is approved. The candidate registry was not read in this run, so overlap with existing candidates is unchecked.

Principles 9 and 10 (avoid agents where deterministic automation suffices; keep the agent set as small as possible) apply to this capability and point away from a standing multi-agent design.

Aggregation, clustering by existing attributes and joining to change and lineage context is deterministic work and should be a deterministic process that produces a curated evidence packet, not agent work.

The hypothesis-drafting step should be read-only on the approved packet only, with no direct read access to raw exception, change or lineage records, consistent with minimum permissions and read-and-recommend.
The workflow's output must stay at hypothesis level with visible uncertainty and must not declare a root cause or resolve an operational incident.
The capability is classified as an AI-assisted workflow with a redesign verdict for the candidate 'Exception & Root-Cause Agent'.

Approval of each curated evidence packet, final root-cause determination, any production or threshold change, and sign-off of this design remain human decisions.
